snapshot: Nikkei 225 futures opened at 64,170 at 08:45 JST, up 830 from the prior weekend settlement. Cash equities also opened higher.
By 09:36 JST the Nikkei had climbed to 65,018.07, breaking above the 65,000 line for the first time.
Reuters' pre-open range was 62,900-63,600, but Middle East peace hopes and AI-semiconductor buying drove a clear upside break.
Crude fell below $100 on U.S.-Iran peace hopes and the dollar softened, temporarily easing Japan's import-cost concerns.
The U.S. market is scheduled to close for Memorial Day, so after the first wave of buying, the key issue is whether stock-specific catalysts can keep working.

drivers.driver: Oil down and futures up on Middle East peace hopes
drivers.why_today: Expectations that the Strait of Hormuz could reopen pushed crude sharply lower and Nikkei futures higher. The easing in import-cost pressure is lifting Japanese risk appetite.

drivers.driver: AI and semiconductor leadership accelerated again
drivers.why_today: Kioxia and SoftBank Group are helping push the Nikkei into the 65,000 area. Buying remains concentrated in large AI and semiconductor-linked names.
Quantum Solutions, Qualtec, Sato Shoji, Cyber Security Cloud and A&A Material all have easy-to-check disclosures, giving the open a stock-picking layer as well.

deep_dive.title: Kioxia: can the leader of the Nikkei 65,000 breakout keep control after the open

lines: Kioxia is today's key name because it combines index contribution and a powerful AI-memory theme.
The stock is resisting weakness in U.S. peer SanDisk and continues to trade as the strongest domestic semiconductor leader.
As the Nikkei broke above 65,000 for the first time, Kioxia was confirmed alongside SoftBank Group as a major driver of the move.
Crude's decline on Middle East peace hopes improved the broader tape, allowing AI and data-center names to attract fresh risk capital.
Can the stock hold the 60,000-yen area and remain among the highest-turnover names.
Can it outperform Tokyo Electron and Advantest inside the semiconductor group.
Weak U.S. memory-stock performance starts feeding through to Japanese peers.
Profit-taking after the sharp rally prevents the stock from holding its morning high zone.
The stock is heavily extended in the short term, so a futures-led reversal could produce a fast pullback.
With the U.S. market closed for Memorial Day, afternoon liquidity may thin and make high levels harder to sustain.
